_comment: The people of each book, in order of appearance: name, when, one line from the essay, and a picture from the library (book whose scans may be shared). Without a picture, the person gets the woodcut initial of their name. Captions say what the picture is: a later book's imagining is not a likeness.

sea-road-china-gulf.name: Cristóvão da Costa
sea-road-china-gulf.line: Remembered in his book of drugs that four hundred Chinese ships once came into Hormuz on a single tide.

pic.caption: Black pepper, from his book of drugs (1578)

sea-road-china-gulf.name: Sulayman the Merchant
sea-road-china-gulf.line: A merchant of the China voyage, whose sailing directions survive in Ibn al-Faqih’s geography.

sea-road-china-gulf.name: Ibn Khordadbeh
sea-road-china-gulf.line: Ran the caliph’s post and intelligence service, and listed the route to China stage by stage.

sea-road-china-gulf.name: Ibn Rustah
sea-road-china-gulf.line: Graded the world’s musk: the best Chinese musk came by sea from Khanfu.

sea-road-china-gulf.name: al-Qazwini
sea-road-china-gulf.line: A judge of Qazvin whose Wonders of Creation gathered the marvels of the China Sea.

sea-road-china-gulf.name: Zhao Rugua
sea-road-china-gulf.line: Inspector of Foreign Trade, who wrote down what the foreign merchants in his port told him.

sea-road-china-gulf.name: Marco Polo
sea-road-china-gulf.line: Sailed the whole road from China with fourteen ships and came ashore at Hormuz.

pic.caption: Marco Polo as Münster’s Cosmographey (1598) pictured him

sea-road-china-gulf.name: Ibn Battuta
sea-road-china-gulf.line: Envoy of the Sultan of Delhi to China, who waited three months at Calicut for the season to sail.

sea-road-china-gulf.name: Zheng He
sea-road-china-gulf.line: Led seven Ming fleets into the Indian Ocean, to Calicut and Hormuz.

pic.caption: The start of his route, on the chart printed in the Wubei zhi (1621)

sea-road-china-gulf.name: Jan Huyghen van Linschoten
sea-road-china-gulf.line: The Dutch traveller whose Itinerario showed Europe the Portuguese Indies.

pic.caption: Linschoten at thirty-two, from his Itinerario (1596)

sea-road-china-gulf.name: Wei Yuan
sea-road-china-gulf.line: Compiled the Illustrated Treatise on the Maritime Kingdoms after the Opium War, when the road had turned against China.

pic.caption: A map of southern Asia from his Treatise

hyperborea.name: Pindar
hyperborea.line: Put Hyperborea at the limit of human striving: neither by ship nor by land is the road found.

hyperborea.name: Herodotus
hyperborea.line: Heard of the straw-wrapped offerings at Delos, and was the first to doubt the Hyperboreans.

hyperborea.name: Abaris
hyperborea.line: The one Hyperborean with a name: a priest of Apollo who came south gathering gold.

hyperborea.name: Pythagoras
hyperborea.line: In Iamblichus, showed Abaris his golden thigh, to prove he was Apollo.

pic.caption: Pythagoras, from Manly P. Hall’s Secret Teachings of All Ages (1928)

hyperborea.name: Iamblichus
hyperborea.line: Gave Abaris a career in his Life of Pythagoras.

hyperborea.name: The Heliades
hyperborea.line: Phaethon’s sisters, who wept by the Eridanus until they became poplars and their tears amber.

hyperborea.name: Pytheas of Massalia
hyperborea.line: Sailed north past Britain and reported Thule, where the midsummer sun did not set.

hyperborea.name: William Stukeley
hyperborea.line: Saw Hecataeus’s round temple of the Hyperboreans in Stonehenge.

pic.caption: A trilithon, drawn by Stukeley himself

hyperborea.name: Olof Rudbeck
hyperborea.line: Made Sweden both Plato’s Atlantis and Hyperborea.

hyperborea.name: Christoph Hartknoch
hyperborea.line: Read the Greeks’ amber river as his own Prussian coast.

pic.caption: Hartknoch, from his Old and New Prussia (1684)

hyperborea.name: Teodor Narbutt
hyperborea.line: Found the Hyperborean Apollo in a Baltic sun cult, and Lithuanian in Sanskrit.

pic.caption: Burial mounds in Samland, from his history

hyperborea.name: Helena Blavatsky
hyperborea.line: Made the Hyperboreans the second of her root races, and the amber her proof.

pic.caption: Blavatsky, a photograph reproduced in The Phoenix (1931)
